paper: Mollova et al. 2023, Microorganisms 11(10):2440 — L. plantarum PU3 (Nanopore)

open_questions.q: Does the deposited Nanopore-only PU3 assembly carry a residual homopolymer indel error rate that would shift any CDS boundaries or introduce truncated ORFs if paired short-read (Illumina) data were used for hybrid polishing?
open_questions.basis: The paper assembles with Flye v2.9.2 on Oxford Nanopore MinION R9.4.1 reads, polished with Racon v1.4.21 + Medaka v1.8.1. No Illumina reads were used at any stage. R9.4.1 chemistry has a well-documented residual homopolymer indel bias even after Medaka polishing, and this could plausibly explain part of the ~25% CDS-count spread across Prokka/PGAP/BV-BRC (3,273 / 3,617 / 3,794 vs paper 2,874) if a subset of ORFs are being called as frameshifted pseudogenes by one pipeline and full-length CDSs by another.
next_steps: Check NCBI SRA for any subsequent Illumina resequencing of strain PU3 (BioProject PRJNA946199 or related).
If no short reads exist, request them from the Plovdiv group; ~1 lane of NovaSeq is inexpensive.
Run hybrid polishing (Pilon or POLCA) with Illumina reads and diff the resulting CDS set against the deposited genome; count changed CDS boundaries and new/removed ORFs.
Report per-plasmid indel-correction counts, since the 3.5 kb PPU3_9 plasmid is small enough that a single indel materially shifts annotation.

open_questions.q: Are the small ORFs at 30–50 aa inside the chromosome 1,561,101–1,586,810 bacteriocin window actually the mature Plantaricin E, F, and K core peptides, or are some of them unrelated small hypothetical ORFs that Prodigal called opportunistically?
open_questions.basis: The paper (via BAGEL4) reports PlnE/F/K core peptides plus PlnT/U/V/W accessories at this window. Our Prokka run confirmed the regulatory + transport + secretion machinery (AgrA, LagD×2, LcnD) at the exact coordinates and found small hypothetical ORFs in the correct 30–50 aa size class, but Prokka's default DB does not carry plantaricin core-peptide HMMs. Whether every small ORF Prodigal called is a genuine bacteriocin, an immunity peptide, or a spurious call is not resolved here.
next_steps: Install BAGEL4 locally (Docker image available) and run it on CP120642.1 to get direct PlnE/F/K/T/U/V/W labels.
BLASTp each small ORF in the window against a curated bacteriocin database (BACTIBASE or BAGEL4's internal DB).
Cross-check with antiSMASH bacteriocin/RiPP module for cluster-boundary agreement.
Look for canonical double-glycine leader peptides (GG-motif) upstream of each small ORF — hallmark of class II bacteriocins including plantaricins.

open_questions.q: Does PU3 actually produce active plantaricin (i.e., bacteriocin activity in a spot-on-lawn assay against a susceptible indicator like L. monocytogenes or another L. plantarum), or is the cluster present-but-silent (cryptic) as is common in Lactobacillus?
open_questions.basis: Presence of a bacteriocin biosynthesis cluster in the genome does not entail active production. Many sequenced L. plantarum strains carry pln clusters that are transcriptionally silent under standard MRS growth, requiring induction by cell-to-cell contact via the AgrA/PlnA quorum-sensing peptide or by cocultivation with an inducer strain. The paper reports the cluster genomically but this replication (and, so far as we can tell, the paper) did not test whether the cluster is actually expressed and functional in PU3.
next_steps: Request PU3 from the Plovdiv group (or purchase from a strain repository if deposited).
Perform standard spot-on-lawn / well-diffusion assay against L. monocytogenes, L. plantarum WCFS1 (potentially susceptible), and Enterococcus faecalis.
If no activity, coculture with a known inducer (e.g., L. plantarum C11 supernatant carrying PlnA) and re-test.
RT-qPCR on plnE/plnF transcripts in exponential vs stationary phase to see whether the cluster is transcribed at all under lab conditions.

open_questions.q: Are any of the 9 PU3 plasmids required for probiotic-relevant phenotypes (bile tolerance, adhesion, bacteriocin production), or are they all dispensable — and does the conjugative plasmid (per MOB-Typer) pose a horizontal-gene-transfer safety concern in a probiotic destined for infant use given the breast-milk origin?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports MOB-Typer classification of 4 mobilizable + 4 non-mobilizable + 1 conjugative plasmid. It does not test plasmid function or curing. Given the strain is proposed as a probiotic isolated from human breast milk, plasmid dispensability and HGT potential are directly relevant to safety and mechanism-of-action claims. The zero-VF/zero-acquired-AMR result (C10) is reassuring but does not by itself close the HGT question.
next_steps: Attempt plasmid curing (novobiocin sub-MIC serial passage; ethidium bromide; elevated temperature) to obtain plasmid-loss derivatives.
Re-test bile / acid / adhesion / bacteriocin phenotypes on cured derivatives to assess plasmid contribution.
For the conjugative plasmid: filter-mating assay with a marker-carrying recipient (e.g., E. faecalis JH2-2) to measure actual transfer frequency in vitro.
Deep-sequence the conjugative plasmid for any mobile-element cargo that could pick up AMR genes in vivo.

open_questions.q: Does the 99.6% ANI to L. plantarum M19 (raw-milk motal cheese isolate) reflect deep phylogenetic proximity — i.e., is PU3 a bona fide independent isolate, or could it be a re-isolation / cross-contamination of an existing dairy strain that reached the donor mother through diet?
open_questions.basis: 99.60–99.61% ANI is close to the intra-species ceiling for L. plantarum and is notably closer than to the type strain WCFS1 (98.6%). M19 was isolated from raw-milk motal cheese (a Caucasus dairy product). PU3 was isolated from human breast milk of a Bulgarian donor. The mother's diet was not reported. Whether PU3 is a true breast-milk-native isolate, a diet-derived transient, or a laboratory cross-contamination cannot be resolved from ANI alone. This matters for the paper's central 'novel probiotic from human breast milk' framing.
next_steps: Compute a core-genome SNP tree of PU3, M19, WCFS1, and 20+ other L. plantarum isolates from breast-milk vs dairy vs plant vs GI sources using ParSNP or Snippy-core.
Estimate divergence time under a molecular clock; if PU3 and M19 diverged <100 years ago it strongly suggests recent common ancestry (i.e., dietary transfer).
Look for shared mobile elements / plasmids between PU3 and M19 that would indicate very recent shared environment.
Ask the Plovdiv group whether the donor's dietary history was recorded and whether traditional dairy consumption was routine.
Chain-of-custody audit: was M19 handled in any lab that later handled PU3?
